title: ZZWF07 7-round AES-192 Related-key differential-linear / first

target.description: AES-192 first7 rounds, finalMC omitted. 20 guessed bytes:16 bytes k7 plus4 bytes w6. No independently quantified192-bit-master-key completion at this budget.

setting.key_relation: Two unknown master keys with XOR ((0,0,0,0),(0,0,0,0),(a,0,0,0),(a,0,0,0),0,0); a chosen nonzero.
setting.plaintext_model: Chosen plaintext observations under two unknown keys with the stated XOR relation.
assumptions: The literal procedure selects maximum absolute parity deviation among subkey candidates; source component-count bias and Matsui rule of thumb do not quantify all candidate-ranking failures.

The exact11/5440 bias is a count over uniformly weighted compatible intermediate tuples, not a proof that every fixed related AES key pair induces that distribution. After SR and equivalent-key addition the signed bias is multiplied by (-1)^{lambda dot (Delta w[13] XOR Delta w[10])}; its absolute model bias is unchanged.

time.note: Section5.2 reports 2^187 after 127 possible b branches rounded to 2^7, reusing the 2^22 plaintext blocks. Arithmetic 2^160*2^22*(2/7)*127 has log2=187.1813; this refines rounding, not a new attack.

data.note: Source aggregate block count across both keys; Matsui heuristic and the stated construction.

memory.note: Literal Section5.1 step3 array of 2^160 counters; counter width and peak ciphertext storage not numerically specified. The 127 b branches are not reported as simultaneously resident.

preprocessing.note: No numerical amount is reported for this resource.

success.description: No numerical success probability for the recorded partial-key ranking output is supplied. The source uses approximately2^-9 bias and the Matsui rule8*(2^-9)^-2≈2^21 pairs; a sample-size rule is not a finite-budget success probability. Unknown parity sign is handled by the highest/lowest-extremum ranking; no trial denominator or correct-rank distribution is reported. No later-paper95% rate is borrowed.

components.description: Equation6 (or the shifted Equation10 construction with its own key relation and input conditions): the designated two byte differences are equal and nonzero at the specified boundary. This deterministic conditioned relation is not key-ranking success.

Equation7: exact count for uniformly sampled compatible pre-key-offset tuples. The bias is11/5440 (about2^-9); correlation is twice the bias. A fixed key XOR offset can flip the parity sign, so this is not a universal post-key zero-parity probability or the probability that the correct counter wins.

review.scope: Exact-edition endpoint-specific success audit. Local collision, table-hit, conditional retention and filter events are separate from recovery success or distinguishing advantage. Existing costs, targets, settings, conflicts and full-audit gates remain unchanged.
